audit.verification: Admitted as a Los Angeles story location: AFI places the film in Los Angeles and describes the station interrogation, T-800 attack, officers killed and Sarah/Reese escape. Copied the existing The Terminator canonical-time object verbatim: 1984, explicit year; no invented month/day.

Primary name Central Division comes from the inspected 1984 entrance-frame door. T2 revised shooting-script scene 59A retrospectively calls the 1984 station West Highland (singular); West Highlands appears in some location listings. T2 supplies retrospective name/death-count corroboration, not a second physical-location appearance. None of these names is treated as a verified street address or real neighborhood.

Paul H’s Halloween Filming Locations research identifies a dressed, disused Bethlehem Steel office at 6000 S Boyle Avenue, Vernon, from a production document. It reports demolition of the office/plant in 1985. Reel to Real credits Paul and pairs the entrance frame with a historical 6000 Boyle Avenue photograph. These identify the police-station office, not the separate final factory at Ramirez Street / City of Industry.

The pin is a former-site approximation taken from HFL’s linked map, which resolves to 33.9871716, -118.2119171. The current Census address match is -118.212668921045, 33.988186316747, roughly 130 m away. Redevelopment and historical address ambiguity prevent building-level precision. Both points lie inside the aerial coverage; neither establishes the fictional police station’s street.

Seventeen dead is supported by T2 scene 59A’s explicit dialogue, not Traxler’s earlier reassurance that thirty cops were in the building. No list of seventeen invented identities is added. The single parent place carries event/work/death categories and one deaths record so the app can derive its normal death entry.

Traxler is named using AFI’s Ed Traxler credit; the March 1984 script identifies him as dying in scene 178 after the assault. Vukovich is present and fights, but his death is not explicitly established in the released sequence; earlier drafts swap some Traxler/Vukovich actions, so Vukovich is retained as a workplace character without a certified death. Dr. Peter Silberman exits in scene 160 before the attack and is not a victim.

Visually inspected six police-location source images and the 2025 aerial: frame entrance canopy/doors match the archival office entrance with 6000 Boyle Avenue lettering. Public screen is the real film frame, not the black-and-white historical photograph. Public place image is real World Imagery aerial photography of the redeveloped site; provider metadata explicitly dates capture 2025-11-26. JPEGs optimized without generated content.
